analysis.investment_thesis: Capillary Technologies fails both Magic Formula tests catastrophically — Earnings Yield of ~1.5% (EBIT ₹65 Cr / EV ~₹4,397 Cr) and ROIC of ~2.9% are both far below any acceptable threshold. At 420x P/E for a company that only just turned profitable in FY2025 with ₹13 Cr net profit, the market is pricing in decades of future perfection.
key_strengths: Strong revenue CAGR of 36.7% over 4 years (₹171 Cr → ₹598 Cr), demonstrating genuine top-line momentum
First year of positive EBITDA (₹72 Cr) and operating income (₹65 Cr) in FY2025 signals inflection point
Low leverage (D/E 0.17) and healthy cash balance of ₹201 Cr provide runway to sustain growth investments
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1.5% (EBIT/EV) is 10x below my 15% attractiveness threshold — the stock is spectacularly overpriced
ROIC of 2.88% is a fraction of my 20% minimum; the business destroys value on incremental capital deployed
Free cash flow turned deeply negative in FY2025 (-₹94 Cr) despite the first profitable year — EBIT is not converting to cash, a serious red flag
red_flags: OCF turned negative (-₹46 Cr) in FY2025, the very year EBIT first went positive — suggests accounting profits are not real economic earnings
Cumulative losses of ₹269 Cr over FY2021–2024 before thin ₹13 Cr net profit in FY2025; profitability track record is essentially zero
P/E of 420x and EV/EBITDA of 51.78x assign an extreme premium to a company with no demonstrated sustained earnings power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through the Magic Formula lens, Capillary Technologies is a textbook AVOID. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) calculates to roughly 1.5% — my threshold for "attractive" is 15%, making this stock priced at roughly 10x what I'd consider fair for a good business. Return on Capital at 2.88% (per reported ROCE) is catastrophically low; a business earning less than 3% on its deployed capital is not a "good business" in any sense — it is destroying shareholder wealth with every rupee of growth investment. Both legs of the Magic Formula fail simultaneously, which means the stock scores near the bottom of any ranking I would construct.

The bull narrative centers on the revenue inflection (36.7% CAGR) and first-ever EBIT positivity in FY2025. I acknowledge the growth is real and the business is moving in the right direction. However, the critical warning sign is that even in the first "profitable" year, operating cash flow turned negative at -₹46 Cr and FCF collapsed to -₹94 Cr. This tells me the ₹65 Cr EBIT is not yet translating into economic earnings — likely due to working capital burn or aggressive capitalization of costs. Until ROIC sustainably exceeds 15–20% and earnings yield breaks above 10%, this stock simply cannot appear in a Magic Formula screen at any ranking worth acting on.
